story.head: Who blinks first?
paras: The Lightning won the teams’ first meeting this season, 8-3 in Buffalo on Nov 11. The Lightning have won two in a row, while the Sabres (9-10-4) lost 4-3 to Florida last night. This is an Atlantic Division matchup, with the Sabres sixth (tied for 22nd in the NHL) and the Bolts second (tied for sixth).
This season, the Sabres have been outscored 80-67, but only 49-46 at 5-on-5. On special teams, opponents have outscored them 24-13.

The Sabres rarely get pinned in their own end (3rd) and get their defensemen shooting (5th), but don’t block many shots (30th). On the other side, the Lightning ice the puck less than almost anyone (3rd), keep shots away from their net (3rd) and draw more penalties than they take (4th). Something has to give when the Lightning’s shooting runs into the Sabres’ defense. On top of that, the Lightning could find some good looks against the Sabres, who give up plenty of them.

Tage Thompson (15 G / 11 A / 26 P in 23 GP) leads the Sabres in scoring, and Jack Quinn (12 G / 11 A / 23 P in 23 GP) is next in line. Nikita Kucherov (9 G / 22 A / 31 P in 22 GP) leads the Lightning in scoring and is tied for ninth in the NHL, with nine points in his last five games and nine goals in twelve games against Buffalo since 2023-24. Jake Guentzel (13 G / 14 A / 27 P in 22 GP) has a team-high 13 goals, tied for tenth in the NHL, with nine points in his last five games.

Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen (6-4-3 / .872 SV% in 12 GS) is expected to start for Buffalo, and Andrei Vasilevskiy (11-5-1 / .895 SV% in 17 GS) for Tampa Bay. Luukkonen has a .847 save percentage in seven starts against the Lightning, well under his usual .901. Don’t read much into it: a goalie’s record against one team rarely holds up.
At home, Jon Cooper likes to send Mikheyev, Cirelli and Holmberg out against the other team’s top line, so watch for them against Benson, Kulich and Thompson.
